failure_analysis.evidence: Failures are scattered across the sequence; two rows successful in R205 failed in R207; all ten have the same completed estimator FLOP count. This is consistent with wall-clock scheduling/cache jitter rather than estimator arithmetic or FLOP exhaustion.

frozen_mitigation.name: single_cpu_affinity
frozen_mitigation.exact_rule: Before the public-50 measurement, choose min(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) and execute the unchanged whest process under taskset -c <that_cpu>. The affinity is inherited by child processes.
frozen_mitigation.rationale: R207 already fixes BLAS/OpenMP threads to one. Pinning that single-threaded process to one allowed CPU removes CPU migration/cache-affinity jitter without changing estimator inputs, code, FLOP accounting, arithmetic, limits, dataset order, or V26_STRASSEN=4.

confirmation.command_template: CPU=$(python -c 'import os; print(min(os.sched_getaffinity(0)))'); taskset -c "$CPU" whest run --estimator methods/r210/estimator_v29.py --dataset hf://aicrowd/arc-whestbench-public-2026@v2-phase2 --split mini --streaming --n-mlps 50 --runner local --flop-budget 2199023255552 --wall-time-limit 120 --residual-wall-time-limit 0.4 --max-threads 1 --format json
